## What it is
The heat pump is a freezer and a heater in one machine, with a catch: it does not make heat, it [bold]moves[/bold] it. It has two pipe connections on opposite ends.
- The [bold]green end[/bold] is the gas port. This is the pipe you are conditioning, and it sits where a freezer's pipe would be. - The [bold]red end[/bold] is the waste port. When the machine cools, this is where the heat goes. When it heats, this is where the heat comes from.
Wire it up, set a target temperature, and it will work out by itself whether it has to cool or heat.
## Why you need a waste loop
A normal freezer in space can throw heat away for free, so it will happily cool a pipe to 73 K with nothing else attached. The heat pump cannot: every joule it takes out of the gas has to end up in the red pipe, and every joule it puts into the gas comes out of the red pipe.
That means the red pipe needs somewhere for the heat to go — a radiator loop, a big tank of gas, or a cold part of the ship — and it needs to actually have gas in it, because gas is what carries the heat. Cooling into a waste loop that is already hot is slow and expensive.
## Efficiency
The machine works best when the waste loop is close to the temperature of the gas. As the waste loop heats up the machine loses efficiency, and it loses a lot more if either pipe is nearly empty — gas is what carries the heat away.
Because it moves heat instead of making it, the heat pump gets more cooling out of a joule than a freezer does, as long as the waste loop can absorb the heat.
Better parts help. The [bold]Upgrades[/bold] entry in the machine's examine menu shows what the installed parts changed:
- [bold]Matter bins[/bold] give the machine more heat capacity, raise the most heat it can move in a second, and make it thriftier with power: the best bins take it from 78 kW to 624 kW, and a full-tilt machine with them draws about 50 kW. - [bold]Manipulators[/bold] raise the floor the efficiency falls back to when the waste loop is hot, from 25% on stock parts to 90% with the best ones, and widen the range of temperatures you can ask for, from 73-593 K to 28-1193 K. They do not help an empty pipe: with no gas to carry the heat, even a fully upgraded machine crawls.
## Safeties
If the waste loop gets hot enough to be dangerous, the heat pump shuts itself down. The safeties can be switched off from the interface, and an emagged machine has them off already — at that point the waste loop keeps climbing, and eventually the machine gives up and explodes.
